haiku-low.q1: Row count of 10,000 or fewer returns the CSV directly as 200 text/csv. Above 10,000, it records an export row, enqueues a background job, returns 202 JSON, and emails a 24-hour link later.
haiku-low.q2: The second click returns the existing export as 202 with its status, filters and cols. No second export starts, and the page shows which view it covers.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours. The bucket's 7-day delete rule removes the stored file. The plan adds no cleanup job.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts in total. After the final failure, the row is set to failed, the page shows failed, and an export_failed email is sent.
haiku-low.q5: Report rows come only from the read replica, never the primary. The primary is used only for export bookkeeping and the status lookup.
haiku-low.q6: Stored in the report_exports row on the primary. The page polls the latest-status endpoint every 5 seconds while queued or running, and page load fetches it again.
haiku-low.q7: Streams 5,000-row pages from the read replica, writes CSV into an 8 MiB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part.
haiku-low.q8: Attempt failure aborts the upload; nothing becomes visible. Each retry restarts from zero. A killed worker's upload is discarded by the bucket after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q9: The browser sends filters and cols on click. They are stored as raw text in the report_exports row and passed in the enqueue payload to the job.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status is queued or running, used by INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the primary.
haiku-low.q11: Upload completion and a done row come first. A rerun with done but no emailed_at only resends the email. If emailed_at is set, it returns.
haiku-low.q12: Error before sending returns 500 with no file. The body is built fully first, so no partial CSV downloads; the user clicks again.

sonnet.q1: The click endpoint reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total, from the replica). If <=10,000, the response is the CSV directly (200 text/csv attachment, built in memory, nothing stored). If >10,000, it records an export row, enqueues a background job and returns 202 with the export row; the user later gets an emailed link.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running makes the insert skip; no second export starts. The endpoint returns the existing export row as 202 (export_id, status, filters, cols), even if the new click had different filters; the page shows which view it covers.
sonnet.q3: The link is valid 24 hours (signed_url 86400 seconds, generated at send time). The bucket's own rule deletes the object 7 days after creation.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts total (waits of 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3). After the last failure on_final_failure sets the row to failed (with error, finished_at); the page shows 'failed' and the button works again, and the user is emailed the export_failed message (best effort; if the email fails the page still shows failed).
sonnet.q5: The read replica (for report rows, in both small and large paths). The primary is used only for export bookkeeping (report_exports table).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary database (status queued/running/done/failed). The page reads GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on page load, after a 202, and via a 5-second poll while queued/running; the row persists, so reopening later shows the latest state. Polling stops at done or failed.
sonnet.q7: It streams: fetches 5,000-row keyset pages from the replica, encodes into an in-memory buffer, uploads each 8 MiB buffer as a multipart part and empties it, then uploads the remainder as the last part. Memory is about 20 MB; about 113 parts for 900 MB. It never holds the whole report.
sonnet.q8: On an exception the job calls abort_multipart and re-raises; if the worker dies, the incomplete upload is discarded by the bucket rule after 24 hours. Nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart, so no partial file can be downloaded. The queue keeps no progress, so the next attempt restarts from the beginning (after=0, new multipart upload).
sonnet.q9: The page sends filters and cols (raw values from the URL) in the click request. They are stored as text in the report_exports row and also placed in the enqueue payload (export_id, user_id, report_id, filters, cols), which the job receives and re-parses.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') combined with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the primary; only one insert succeeds and the other gets the existing row back.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have succeeded and the row been updated to done (file_key, finished_at); the signed URL is then generated and the email sent, then emailed_at is set. On rerun: status failed means return; done with emailed_at set means return (no second email); done with emailed_at NULL means skip rebuild and only send the email.
sonnet.q12: The CSV body is fully built in memory before sending, so any error returns 500 with no file; a half-finished download cannot occur. If the 60-second limit is exceeded the user gets an error. The user can click again; nothing is stored.
